new_events.summary: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met U.S. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper in Jeddah to discuss regional developments amid Houthi escalation.

Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority published an updated list of 77 vessels it said violated Iranian Hormuz protocols and announced possible fines, detention or confiscation. It also warned insurers, P&I clubs and classification societies against servicing listed vessels. External legal recognition or compliance was not established.

new_events.actor: Unknown attacker / Iranian Kurdish opposition camps
new_events.summary: Kurdistan Region security reporting said five missiles struck three areas in Sulaimani province, including a camp associated with Iranian Kurdish opposition groups. No casualties were reported. Attribution remained unresolved in reviewed sources.

new_events.actor: United States / Iran / Austria / UN sanctions committee
new_events.summary: Iran protested after nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami was prevented from attending the IAEA General Conference. Reuters reported Austria sought a UN sanctions travel exemption and the committee did not approve it after a U.S. objection.
Iranian state media reported senior Sunni cleric Molavi Yusef Gorgij was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in southeastern Iran. Attacker identity and motive remained unresolved.

existing_event_updates.summary: AP reported the East-West pipeline will remain mostly out of service for roughly three to five weeks during repairs. This updates the prior damaged/still-shut state and does not create a new attack occurrence.
AP reporting confirmed Houthi control of Greater and Lesser Hanish. This upgrades the earlier evidence wording without recounting the Sep. 10-11 territorial advance as a new Sep. 14 occurrence.

Reuters preliminary tracking counted four commodity vessels exiting and ten entering the Gulf over the weekend, below the recent 10-day average. AIS-dark vessels may be missing from preliminary counts.
Reuters tracking counted 24 Bab el-Mandeb vessel transits Saturday and 27 Sunday, approximately in line with the recent 10-day average. A general closure was not established at this cutoff.
IOM reporting put displacement since Sep. 1 at 82,164 people, with more than 2,000 people fleeing to Djibouti.
Saudi Civil Defense issued and later lifted danger alerts for Najran, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Abha. New successful impacts or BDA were not established by reviewed sources.
No Treasury/OFAC action identifying the announced large bank was found by the 12:01 ET cutoff.

claims_and_corrections.claim: Saudi Arabia requested postponement of the planned Oman Gulf-Iran Hormuz meeting.

economic_energy_updates.observed_state: Reuters reported Brent at $109.29/bbl and WTI at $104.26/bbl at 10:15 a.m. EDT, both up more than 4%.
Reuters reported Asian refiners expecting tighter sour crude supply, with at least one Saudi loading delayed; Gulf-to-Asia tanker rates were at records and some Red Sea-loading vessels were AIS-dark.

unresolved_questions: What specific amendments did Saudi Arabia submit to the Iran-Oman Hormuz proposal?
Will Saudi Arabia or Oman independently confirm that Riyadh requested the meeting postponement?
What substantive Hormuz terms, if any, have Oman and Iran agreed to?
Will any GCC state recognize Iran's asserted Strait Authority or 77-vessel list?
Will maritime insurers, P&I clubs or classification societies act on Iran's warning?
Can the Saudi East-West pipeline be partially restored before the 3-5 week estimate?
Who ordered the Sep. 11 Saudi pipeline attack beyond the established Iraqi launch origin?
Who launched the Sep. 14 missiles in Sulaimani province?
Will Houthi territorial control reduce general Bab el-Mandeb traffic?
Which large bank will Treasury designate and when will OFAC enact the action?

limitations: No direct subscription-only AIS, proprietary satellite tasking, P&I circular or classification-society feed was accessible.
Saudi/Omani primary confirmation of Iran's Saudi-delay attribution was not found.
Unverified actor claims were preserved as claims rather than promoted to facts.
